713311.t: From Proto-Hellenic *pʰáňňō, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰh₂-n-yé-ti, thematic yé-present of *bʰeh₂- (“to shine”) with an innovative zero-grade nasal infix. The present tense system includes a *-ϳ- (*-j-) progressive aspect marker.

713323.t: Compound of φαλός (phalós, “white”) + ἄκρος (ákros, “topmost”). Akin to φάλαρος (phálaros).

713309.t: The stem is φαιδ- (phaid-), from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰh₂eyd- (“bright, clear”), whence also Lithuanian gaidrùs (“bright, clear”), gaidrà (“cloudless heaven, clear weather”), giẽdras (“clear, serene”).

713320.t: Traditionally from Proto-Indo-European *bʰelǵ- (“beam, plank”), with cognates such as Latin sufflāmen and Old High German balcho, but regular derivation of φάλαγγ- (phắlăng-) from this root is phonetically impossible, and the suffix is prototypical of…

713347.t: From φάντασις (phắntăsĭs) + -ία (-ĭ́ā), from φαντάζω (phăntắzō, “to make visible”), from φαίνω (phaínō, “to shine”).

713375.t: According to Frisk an inherited Indo-European word for “throat, gorge”, cognate to Latin frūmen and Old Armenian երբուծ (erbuc), both from Proto-Indo-European *bʰruHg- (“to use, enjoy”), but phonetically this is somewhat problematic as the Greek form…

713317.t: Disputed. From a root *bʰaḱ- shared with Albanian bathë (“broad bean”).

713369.t: Unclear etymology, but most likely derived from Proto-Hellenic *pʰármakon. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀞𐀔𐀒 (pa-ma-ko /⁠pʰármakon⁠/).

713398.t: Perhaps from Proto-Hellenic *pā́uros, from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂w-, the irregular φ- (ph-) representing an expressive *pʰ-, as in Old Armenian փոքր (pʻokʻr, “small”).

713342.t: From φαίνω (phaínō, “to show, make visible, bring to light”) + -ρός (-rós).

713391.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ- (“to tie”), the same root of Sanskrit बन्ध॑ति (bándhati) and Proto-Germanic *bindaną. The same suffix is recognized in Gaulish benna and Welsh ben (“cart”).

713351.t: According to Beekes, from Pre-Greek; compare σῆραγξ (sêrănx) and φάλαγξ (phắlănx). Furnée compares also μάραγοι (máragoi, “overhanging places”) and Spanish barranca (“ravine”).

713364.t: It has been assumed a derivation with a reduced grade from φέρω (phérō, “to carry”), beside a full grade in φέρετρον (phéretron, “bier, litter”).

713385.t: From φαίνω (phaínō, “to bring to light, to cause to appear”) + -μα (-ma, nominal suffix) with -σ- from analogy to other -αίνω : -ασμα or from φάσις (phásis).
